content: 1. Deflazacort: When co-administered with strong CYP3A4 and/or P-gp inhibitors, reduce the deflazacort dose to one-third of the recommended dose. Monitor therapy closely. 2. Degarelix and Itraconazole: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor the patient. 3. Itraconazole and Desipramine: Both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor the patient. 4. Deutetrabenazine and Itraconazole: Both increase the QTc interval. At the maximum recommended dose, deutetrabenazine does not prolong the QT interval to a clinically significant extent. However, certain conditions (e.g., bradycardia, hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, congenital QT prolongation, or co-administration with other QT-prolonging drugs) may increase the risk of torsades de pointes or sudden death. Use caution and monitor the patient. 5. Itraconazole and Dexamethasone: Itraconazole increases dexamethasone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while dexamethasone decreases itraconazole levels. Use caution and monitor therapy. 6. Itraconazole and Diazepam: Itraconazole increases diazepam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 7. Didanosine and Itraconazole: Didanosine decreases itraconazole levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Administer itraconazole two hours before or several hours after didanosine. Use caution and monitor therapy. 8. Dienogest/Estradiol Valerate and Itraconazole: Itraconazole increases the levels of these hormones by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for adverse effects such as nausea, irregular uterine bleeding, breast tenderness, and headache. 9. Digoxin and Itraconazole: Itraconazole increases digoxin levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein. Monitor closely. 10. Diltiazem and Itraconazole: Itraconazole increases diltiazem levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Calcium channel blockers (CCBs) may have additive negative inotropic effects with itraconazole. Monitor for adverse reactions and consider dose reduction. 11. Dolasetron and Itraconazole: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor the patient. 12. Donepezil and Itraconazole: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor the patient. 13. Doravirine and Itraconazole: Itraconazole increases doravirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration may increase plasma concentrations and toxicities of doravirine. Use caution and monitor therapy. 14. Doxepin and Itraconazole: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Itraconazole also increases doxepin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 15. Doxorubicin Liposomal and Itraconazole: Itraconazole increases doxorubicin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein. Use caution and monitor therapy. 16. Dronabinol and Itraconazole: Itraconazole increases dronabinol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 17. Dutasteride and Itraconazole: Itraconazole increases dutasteride levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 18. Duvelisib and Itraconazole: Itraconazole increases duvelisib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the duvelisib dose to 15 mg twice daily when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitor closely for toxicities. 19. Elagolix and Itraconazole: Itraconazole increases elagolix levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration of elagolix 200 mg twice daily with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors for more than one month is not recommended. Monitor therapy closely. 20. Eluxadoline and Itraconazole: Itraconazole increases eluxadoline levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 21. Elvitegravir and Itraconazole: Itraconazole increases elvitegravir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Limit the itraconazole dose to 200 mg/day when co-administered with elvitegravir. Monitor therapy closely. 22. Enfortumab Vedotin and Itraconazole: Itraconazole increases the toxicity of enfortumab vedotin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for signs of toxicities. 23. Erythromycin and Itraconazole: Erythromycin increases itraconazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein. Use caution and monitor therapy. 24. Escitalopram and Itraconazole: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Itraconazole also increases escitalopram levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 25. Estradiol and Itraconazole: Itraconazole increases estradiol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein. Use caution and monitor therapy. 26. Ethinyl Estradiol and Itraconazole: Itraconazole increases ethinyl estradiol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase plasma hormone levels. Use caution and monitor therapy. 27. Ethosuximide and Itraconazole: Itraconazole increases ethosuximide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 28. Etoposide and Itraconazole: Itraconazole increases etoposide levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein. Use caution and monitor therapy. 29. Etravirine and Itraconazole: Itraconazole increases etravirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose adjustments may be necessary depending on the co-administered drugs. Monitor therapy closely. 30. Fingolimod and Itraconazole: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor therapy. 31. Flecainide and Itraconazole: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor therapy. 32. Fluoxetine and Itraconazole: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor therapy. 33. Fluticasone and Itraconazole: Itraconazole increases fluticasone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 34. Gefitinib and Itraconazole: Itraconazole increases gefitinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase the risk of gefitinib adverse effects. Monitor therapy closely. 35. Granisetron and Itraconazole: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor therapy. 36. Haloperidol and Itraconazole: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Itraconazole also increases haloperidol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 37. Hydroxyzine and Itraconazole: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor therapy. 38. Ivacaftor and Itraconazole: Itraconazole increases ivacaftor levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the ivacaftor dose when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Refer to specific product guidelines for dosage adjustments. 39. Lapatinib and Itraconazole: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. If concurrent use is unavoidable, decrease the lapatinib dose to 500 mg once daily. Adjust the dose if itraconazole is discontinued. 40. Leuprolide and Itraconazole: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor therapy. 41. Levothyroxine and Itraconazole: Itraconazole increases levothyroxine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 42. Losartan and Itraconazole: Itraconazole decreases losartan effects by inhibiting its metabolism to the active metabolite E-3174. Monitor therapeutic response and adjust losartan dosage as needed. 43. Lumacaftor/Ivacaftor and Itraconazole: Itraconazole increases ivacaftor levels. When initiating lumacaftor/ivacaftor in patients taking strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, reduce the dose to one tablet daily for the first week, then continue with the recommended dose. No adjustment is needed for moderate or weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. 44. Maraviroc and Itraconazole: Itraconazole increases maraviroc levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein. Reduce the maraviroc dose to 150 mg twice daily when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitor therapy closely. 45. Mifepristone and Itraconazole: Both drugs increase each other's levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Do not exceed 300 mg/day of mifepristone for Cushing syndrome when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitor for increased concentrations and toxic effects during and two weeks after treatment. 46. Mitotane and Itraconazole: Mitotane decreases itraconazole levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor therapy and adjust dosages as needed. 47. Modafinil and Itraconazole: Itraconazole increases modafinil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 48. Mometasone and Itraconazole: Itraconazole increases mometasone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. This summary provides a detailed explanation of the interactions between itraconazole and other drugs, emphasizing the need for dose adjustments, monitoring, and caution in specific scenarios.
